title: Understanding LLM performance degradation: a deep dive into Context Window limits
summary: This post explores how Large Language Models experience performance degradation as they approach their context window limits through practical testing with GPT-4.1 and GPT-5. It demonstrates that both models encounter dramatic slowdowns around 400,000 characters and provides strategies for developers to optimize LLM applications by managing context size effectively.
key_points: Context window represents the maximum text an LLM can process in a single request, with measurable impacts on response time and quality
Performance degradation occurs at approximately 400,000 characters for GPT-4.1 and at 600,000+ characters for GPT-5, with response times spiking to 60+ seconds
Attention mechanism complexity scales quadratically with input length, causing exponential increases in computational cost near limits
Developers should stay within 80-85 percent of theoretical token limits and implement context pruning, document chunking, and proper token counting

quotes.text: The context window represents the maximum amount of text (measured in tokens) that an LLM can process in a single request.
quotes.why_it_matters: Defines the fundamental constraint that impacts all LLM application design and performance considerations
